title: U.S. DOJ Rule implementing EO 14117
content: SUMMARY: The Department of Justice is issuing a final rule to implement Executive Order 14117 of February 28, 2024 (Preventing Access to Americans’ Bulk Sensitive Personal Data and United States Government-Related Data by Countries of Concern), by prohibiting and restricting certain data transactions with certain countries or persons.

title: U.S. DOJ Rule implementing EO 14117
content: ## 28 CFR § 202.211 (Covered person)

title: U.S. DOJ Rule implementing EO 14117
content: (a) Definition. The term covered person means: (1) A foreign person that is an entity that is 50% or more owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, by one or more countries of concern or persons described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section; or that is organized or chartered under the laws of, or has its principal place of business in, a country of concern; (2) A foreign person that is an entity that is 50% or more owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, by one or more persons described in paragraphs (a)(1), (3), (4), or (5) of this section; (3) A foreign person that is an individual who is an employee or contractor of a country of concern or of an entity described in paragraphs (a)(1), (2), or (5) of this section; (4) A foreign person that is an individual who is primarily a resident VerDate Sep 2014 18:55 Jan 07, 2025 Jkt 265001 PO 00000 Frm 00074 Fmt 4701 Sfmt 4700 E:\FR\FM\08JAR2.SGM 08JAR2lotter on DSK11XQN23PROD with RULES2

title: U.S. DOJ Rule implementing EO 14117
content: ## 28 CFR § 202.214 (Data brokerage)

title: U.S. DOJ Rule implementing EO 14117
content: (a) Definition. The term data brokerage means the sale of data, licensing of access to data, or similar commercial transactions, excluding an employment agreement, investment agreement, or a vendor agreement, involving the transfer of data from any person (the provider) to any other person (the recipient), where the recipient did not collect or process the data directly from the individuals linked or linkable to the collected or processed data.

content: Right to limit use and disclosure of sensitive personal information : You can direct businesses to only use your sensitive personal information (for example, your social security number, financial account information, your precise geolocation data, or your genetic data) for limited purposes, such as providing you with the services you requested.

Businesses that are subject to the CCPA have several responsibilities, including responding to consumer requests to exercise these rights and giving consumers certain notices explaining their privacy practices . The CCPA applies to many businesses, including data brokers . CPRA amends the CCPA; it does not create a separate, new law. As a result, our office typically refers to the law as “CCPA” or “CCPA, as amended.” Links to Topics A. GENERAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE CCPA B. RIGHT TO OPT-OUT OF SALE OR SHARING C. DATA BROKERS AND THE CCPA Other Consumer Resources on CCPA Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) These FAQs provide general consumer information about the CCPA and how you can exercise your rights under the CCPA. They are not legal advice, regulatory guidance, or an opinion of the Attorney General. We will update this information periodically. A. GENERAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE CCPA 1. What rights do I have under the CCPA? If you are a California resident, you may ask businesses to disclose what personal information they have about you and what they do with that information, to delete your personal information, to direct businesses not to sell or share your personal information, to correct inaccurate information that they have about you, and to limit businesses’ use and disclosure of your sensitive personal information: Right to know : You can request that a business disclose to you: (1) the categories and/or specific pieces of personal information they have collected about you, (2) the categories of sources for that personal information, (3) the purposes for which the business uses that information, (4) the categories of third parties with whom the business discloses the information, and (5) the categories of information that the business sells or discloses to third parties. You can make a request to know up to twice a year, free of charge. Right to delete : You can request that businesses delete personal information they collected from you and tell their service providers to do the same, subject to certain exceptions (such as if the business is legally required to keep the information). title: DCPD 202200894
content: By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United

title: DCPD 202200894
content: Section 1. Purpose. The United States collects signals intelligence so that its national

title: DCPD 202200894
content: security decisionmakers have access to the timely, accurate, and insightful information necessary

title: DCPD 202200894
content: to advance the national security interests of the United States and to protect its citizens and the

title: DCPD 202200894
content: citizens of its allies and partners from harm. Signals intelligence capabilities are a major reason

title: DCPD 202200894
content: we have been able to adapt to a dynamic and challenging security environment, and the United

title: DCPD 202200894
content: States must preserve and continue to develop robust and technologically advanced signals

title: DCPD 202200894
content: intelligence capabilities to protect our security and that of our allies and partners. At the same

title: DCPD 202200894
content: time, the United States recognizes that signals intelligence activities must take into account that

title: DCPD 202200894
content: all persons should be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their nationality or wherever

title: DCPD 202200894
content: they might reside, and that all persons have legitimate privacy interests in the handling of their

title: DCPD 202200894
content: personal information. Therefore, this order establishes safeguards for such signals intelligence

content: Sec. 2. Signals Intelligence Activities.

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: F I SA S E C TI O N FO R EI G N I N TELLI G EN C E SU RVEI L L ANCE ACT

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: In 2008, Congress enacted Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), a critical

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: intelligence collection authority that enables the Intelligence Community (IC) to collect, analyze,

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: and appropriately share foreign intelligence information about national security threats. Section 702

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: authorizes targeted intelligence collection of specific types of foreign intelligence information—such

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: as information concerning international terrorism or the acquisition of weapons of mass destruction—

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: identified by the Attorney General and the Director of National Intelligence (DNI).

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: Section 702 only permits the targeting of non-United States persons who are reasonably believed to be

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: located outside the United States. United States persons and anyone in the United States may not be

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: targeted under Section 702. Section 702 also prohibits “reverse targeting”—the IC may not target a

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: non-U.S. person located outside the U.S. if the purpose of the collection is to collect information about

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: a United States person or anyone located in the United States.

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: Section 702 is not a bulk collection program; it is a substantial and important targeted intelligence

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: collection program. Every Section 702 targeting decision is individualized and documented, approved

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: pursuant to a multi-step process embodied in specific targeting procedures, and reviewed by an

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: Although all Section 702 targets must be non-United States persons reasonably believed to be located

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: outside the United States, Congress has always recognized that such targets may send an email or have

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: a phone call with a United States person. For this reason, Section 702 requires specific procedures to

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: minimize the acquisition, retention, and sharing of any information concerning United States persons.

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: “Minimize,” however, does not always mean “eliminate” – if, for example, a foreign terrorist indicated

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: that a United States person was a key member of an ongoing terrorist plot, this information would

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: be appropriately shared to allow the FBI to take further investigative steps. Congress also amended

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: Section 702 to require specific procedures to ensure the querying of any Section 702-acquired

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: information is consistent with the Fourth Amendment.

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: The Section 702 program is subject to extensive oversight. The Attorney General must approve

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: the targeting, minimization, and querying procedures, each of which are annually reviewed by the

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court (FISC) for consistency with the FISA statute and the Fourth

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: Amendment. Each of the IC elements involved in the Section 702 program has developed internal

title: FISA Section 702 FISA Resource Library
content: oversight processes and programs to ensure compliance with these procedures. The Department

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: For more than two decades, the Internet and associated information technologies have driven

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: unprecedented innovation, economic value, and improvement in social services. Many of these benefits

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: are fueled by data about individuals that flow through a complex ecosystem. As a result, individuals may

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: not be able to understand the potential consequences for their privacy as they interact with systems,

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: products, and services. At the same time, organizations may not realize the full extent of these

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: consequences for individuals, for society, or for their enterprises, which can affect their brands, their

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: bottom lines, and their future prospects for growth.

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: help organizations protect individuals’ privacy. The Privacy Framework can support organizations in:

content: individuals’ privacy and society as a whole; 1

content: • Fulfilling current compliance obligations, as well as future-proofing products and services to

content: meet these obligations in a changing technological and policy environment; and

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: • Facilitating communication about privacy practices with individuals, business partners,

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: Deriving benefits from data while simultaneously managing risks to individuals’ privacy is not well-suited

title: NIST.CSWP.01162020
content: to one-size-fits-all solutions. Like building a house, where homeowners make layout and design choices

content: while relying on a well-engineered foundation, privacy protection should allow for individual choices, as

content: long as effective privacy risk mitigations are already engineered into products and services. The Privacy
